extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: scientists, science educators, museum curators, and students
extracted.subtask_description: Book reviews and institutional notices (exams, appointments, museum practice) in a scientific journal, offering evaluative guidance on textbooks, museum displays, diagnostic practice, and qualifications for academic posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced textbook pedagogical aim
rubrics_metrics.description: The book is written for students who have already completed an elementary course of Organic Chemistry; the object of the teacher should be, not to multiply sets of a similar kind, but rather to present to the student a broad and general view of the more important branches of the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the 'dictionary arrangement' typical of elementary text-books; adopt a method that allows the writer freedom to bring together related subjects (irrespective of their nature) and to deal thoroughly with important theoretical questions which are often inadequately treated in elementary texts. Target the book to students who have finished elementary work and desire an advanced, synthetic treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding 'dictionary arrangement' in textbooks
rubrics_metrics.description: Textbooks should not adopt a dictionary-like arrangement that fragments the subject into isolated entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer organization that groups related subjects together, enabling deeper theoretical treatment and a coherent view of important branches rather than many repetitive exercises or entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate scope relative to student level
rubrics_metrics.description: A textbook intended as a first-year course for students of not very high scholastic attainments should not 'cover too much ground'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the amount and depth of material is manageable for the intended class; do not attempt to compress too much material (from basics to advanced topics) into a preliminary course where students cannot properly master it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textbook completeness and editorial accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: A good scientific book should include essential apparatus such as an index and accurate references; omission of references and incorrect spelling of authors' names are faults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an index, complete and correct bibliographic references, and accurate spelling of authors' names. Provide adequate illustrations and practical hints where relevant; these elements increase the book's usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bacteriological diagnostic care and differential consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Care is necessary to diagnose plague bacteriologically because other microbes may simulate the plague bacillus (examples: Bacterium bristtilense, B. myxoides).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use careful cultural and pathogenicity testing and consider microbes that morphologically resemble Bacillus pestis; do not rely on morphology alone. Practical laboratory hints and methods for distinguishing simulating organisms are valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support claims with appropriate references and statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Assertions about prophylactic efficacy or other significant claims should be accompanied by relevant references and statistical support (e.g., Bannerman's statistics addressing objections to use of Haffkine prophylactic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting experimental or prophylactic results, cite prior relevant work and statistics that bear on contested points; lack of reference to decisive prior statistics is a weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum exhibition principles for instructing the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens exhibited in galleries should, so far as possible, form a distinct collection adapted specially to its purpose of instructing the general public; old and bad taxidermy should disappear; specimens should not be crowded together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each specimen should be exhibited with a purpose, be instructively or 'descriptively' labelled, and placed so that it can be properly seen. Curators should balance pictorial mounting against the risk of making a 'collection of labels illustrated by specimens' versus 'specimens explained by labels.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Debate on pictorial mounting vs. label-centred displays
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a question as to how far 'pictorial mounting' ought to be adopted in natural history museums versus relying on labels to explain specimens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curators should consider the museum's instructional purpose and audience when choosing between pictorial, heavily staged mounts and more descriptive label-led displays; the balance may vary by institution and exhibit goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner and candidate qualification requirements (university appointments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates for certain examiner posts must be qualified both on the Mathematical and Experimental side (e.g., Examiner in Natural Philosophy including Practical Physics). Appointments are for three or four years with salary and reimbursement of hotel and travelling expenses; applications must lodge required copies and testimonials by a stated deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify clear qualification expectations (subject-matter breadth and practical competence), application procedures (number of copies, testimonials), deadlines, and appointment terms (length, salary, expenses). A Second Examiner may be appointed to assist with marking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Job application qualifications and submission requirements for academic/technical posts
rubrics_metrics.description: Posts (e.g., Assistant in Agricultural Department, Principal of Technical College) specify minimum qualifications: ability to teach particular subjects (bacteriology), graduate of a British university with special qualifications in physical and engineering sciences preferred; applications should include a limited number of recent testimonials and be sent by a deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state subject-specific qualifications, preferred educational background, limit testimonials (e.g., not more than three), provide application deadlines, and indicate where full particulars and lists of duties may be obtained.
